dedupe_keys.name: two echelon capacitated vehicle routing instances with intermediate facilities from saltillo mexico municipal solid waste collection

description: These routing problems describe how rubbish trucks in Saltillo, a city in northern Mexico, collect household waste in the morning shift, unload at transfer stations and hand over to larger vehicles that haul it to the landfill. The producers are Oswaldo Pérez-Luis, Belén Melián-Batista and Marcos Moreno-Vega of the Universidad de La Laguna in Spain and Irma García-Calvillo of the Universidad Autónoma de Coahuila, who derived the instances from the city's real collection system. Each instance has a depot, settlements as customers with demand and service time based on their population, two intermediate transfer facilities where collection and transport vehicles must synchronise, and the landfill. Demand assumes 1.8 kilograms per person per day, with a third of weekly waste collected in the morning shift, and trucks carry up to 12,000 kilograms, so large settlements are split into several nodes. The files are available as a free 7z download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: demand is estimated from population, not weighed, one shift is represented, and file formats are documented briefly. Simulation uses: benchmarking waste collection routing with transfer stations, and testing how closing a transfer station or landfill access road changes collection costs. Related records: SwolfPy (model-swolfpy) models waste system costs and emissions.
